title: Direction Change Between a Retail Fill and a Home Delivery Prescription — Transition Allowance
content:
**Transition allowance (Utilization Management Program, member-filed first-time quantity limit exception requests).** A transition allowance covers a direction change: when the newest home delivery prescription was written after the most recent paid retail fill and directs at least 1.5 times the quantity per 30 days that fill supplied, 2 units are added; when it was written after that fill and directs more than that fill supplied but less than 1.5 times as much, 1 unit is added; otherwise nothing is added. The units are added to the quantity the request asks for.

The prescription is the newest prescription for the drug on file at the Home Delivery Pharmacy, by written date; the fill is the member's most recent paid retail fill of the drug under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. "Written after" means a written date later than the fill's date of service. The quantity per 30 days the prescription directs is its quantity per fill multiplied by 30 and divided by its days supply per fill; the quantity per 30 days the fill supplied is its quantity multiplied by 30 and divided by its days supply.

## Input, judgement, result

| Prescription written after the fill | Prescription's quantity per 30 days compared with the fill's | Units added |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | at least 1.5 times | 2 |
| Yes | more than the fill's, less than 1.5 times | 1 |
| Yes | equal to or less than the fill's | 0 |
| No (same day or earlier) | any | 0 |
| No home delivery prescription on file | — | 0 |

## Hypothetical cases (retail fill of 9 tablets for 30 days, that is 9 per 30 days)

- Prescription written after the fill for 27 tablets per 60-day fill: 13.5 per 30 days, exactly 1.5 times 9 — 2 units.
- Prescription written after the fill for 12 tablets per 30 days: more than 9 and less than 13.5 — 1 unit.
- Prescription for 18 tablets per 30 days written the same day as the fill: not written after it — no units.
